<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, touching **28** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object), runtimeTypes (symbol, a field of const object AUTHORING_RULES))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/build-with-claude-code.mdx`  _(via record_header (literal, a string literal in isButton; a string literal in validateRecordPageHeader))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx`  _(via record_header (literal, a string literal in isButton; a string literal in validateRecordPageHeader), record_more (literal, a string literal in validateRecordPageHeader))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/layout-dsl.mdx`  _(via record_header (literal, a string literal in isButton; a string literal in validateRecordPageHeader), record_more (literal, a string literal in validateRecordPageHeader))_
- `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx`  _(via record_header (literal, a string literal in isButton; a string literal in validateRecordPageHeader), record_more (literal, a string literal in validateRecordPageHeader))_
- `content/docs/ui/pages.mdx`  _(via record_header (literal, a string literal in isButton; a string literal in validateRecordPageHeader), record_more (literal, a string literal in validateRecordPageHeader))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via record_more (literal, a string literal in validateRecordPageHeader))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via record_header (literal, a string literal in isButton; a string literal in validateRecordPageHeader), record_more (literal, a string literal in validateRecordPageHeader))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **67** of **249** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a5a5312ff41dc8cb459b33dbec731c143907db4d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b9f062e420b93bcc93a36c010a90948ced5fb081` — the merge of head `9b06321b8f282348c3f3511616af679bb0b954cd` into base `a5a5312ff41dc8cb459b33dbec731c143907db4d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b9f062e420b93bcc93a36c010a90948ced5fb081 && git checkout b9f062e420b93bcc93a36c010a90948ced5fb081
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a5a5312ff41dc8cb459b33dbec731c143907db4d 9b06321b8f282348c3f3511616af679bb0b954cd && git checkout -B drift-repro a5a5312ff41dc8cb459b33dbec731c143907db4d && git merge --no-ff 9b06321b8f282348c3f3511616af679bb0b954cd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a5a5312ff41dc8cb459b33dbec731c143907db4d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a5a5312ff41dc8cb459b33dbec731c143907db4d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读
按你选的「应用对齐，平台加发布提示」：平台只加了两条提示，页面怎么显示一点没变。应用开发者校验、构建或发布页面时，如果手写记录页的页头标题，或按钮的先后、主按钮，和手机、右侧预览上的不一样，会看到一条黄色提示，发布照常成功。我核过：发布时它只会作为提示返回，没有任何拒绝的路径；它判断按钮顺序的规则和界面实际排按钮的代码一致。HotCRM 主干上已经是 0 条提示，旧版 6.5.0 上正好报出卡里说的线索那两处。
L1 结论：通过（终稿）。这张没有第二道复核，席位可以落地；卡片要等 HotCRM 发版后复查三处再关。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1-d) · repo:objectstack#1 · head `9b06321b` · 2026-11-22T03:45Z

**Face:** `@objectstack/lint` (one advisory rule, its user text, `os explain` text, the registry row, exports) + author docs + four transcript counts. No `packages/spec/src/**`, no `docs/adr/**`, no `ui/`. 808 lines, not governed. `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`; `@objectstack/lint` patch changeset present. No L2 owed, so this is the only review.

**Gates at `9b06321b`:** 63 success, 11 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending; Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check `success`; mergeable clean. `l1-face` clean. The two gates the body marks NOT MEASURED locally (`check:lean-entry-closure`, `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`) are inside CI's lint jobs, all green on this head.

### Against the ruling (7072788648, 「应用对齐，平台加发布提示」)
- Platform behaviour and spec unchanged: the diff touches no renderer and no schema. One publish-time warning for a header `title` other than the object's name field, or an `actions` order contradicting the actions' own order: both ids do exactly that. Short author docs on where the title and primary action are declared: `content/docs/ui/pages.mdx` adds them (object `nameField`, action `order` / `variant: 'primary'`, a slotted page's `header` slot). ✔
- `Part of #36202` is right: the card's HotCRM acceptance waits for a HotCRM release and a recheck, which the ruling and the first line both name. No closing keyword in the body.

### The save door only advises (your first check)
- `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` (`packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts`, end of the function) refuses only findings whose `severity === 'error'`; everything else goes to `advisories`. `RecordPageHeaderFinding.severity` is typed the literal `'warning'` and both `push` sites write `'warning'`, so there is no path to a refusal. The registry row is `tier: 'advisory'`, `runtimeTypes: ['page']`; the test drives a page write through `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` and reads the advisory with no error. ✔

### The action-order estimate against the renderer (your second check)
Read against `ui/packages/components/src/renderers/layout/containers.tsx` on `main`:
- Sort: renderer `(order ?? 0)` ascending, then `variant === 'primary'` first, stable for the rest (2468-2486); its `needsOrdering` short-cut returns the same order a stable sort would. `headerSort` is the same comparator over a stable `Array.prototype.sort`. ✔
- Row vs `⋯`: renderer sends `record_more`-without-`record_header` and `component: 'action:menu'` to the menu, the rest to the row (2652-2659); `isButton` is `record_header` placed and not `action:menu`, the same split for every placed action. ✔
- Primary: renderer's first non-destructive row candidate with `variant: 'primary'`, else the first (2669-2699); `primaryOf` is the same, `variant: 'danger'` excluded (`sys_delete` is a host action, never in an object's `actions`). ✔
- The standard page's set and incoming order: `placedActions: true` / the synthesized header read `placedHeaderActions` = every action placed at `record_header` or `record_more`, in the served object's declaration order (2148-2190). The rule's universe is the object's inline `actions` then the stack's `actions` bound by `objectName`, in source order: an estimate across packages, disclosed in the message, `os explain` and the module note. ✔
- Limits, all disclosed and all in the "quieter" direction except one: visibility / permissions can make it name a difference the runtime hides (HotCRM 6.5.0's `case_detail_page` finding is that case, said in the body). A listed action not placed at `record_header` / `record_more` is dropped from the comparison; the renderer would still draw it from an id list, so the rule is quieter there, never louder. Acceptable for a warning.

### Docs and counts (your third check)
- The four transcripts (`cli.mdx:940`, `validating-metadata.mdx:870`, `build-with-claude-code.mdx:314`, `react-pages.mdx:407`) read 75; `check:docs-transcript-drift` derives the count from the registry and is green; no other "author-time rules (74)" is left in the tree (grepped).
- `pages.mdx` paragraph and the changeset read sentence by sentence against the rule: accurate, including "refusing nothing" and the three named fixes.
- User text: both ids in all 11 platform locales, rendered from real findings by the test; the page-door rule-list pin gains the row in registry order.

### In-repo and HotCRM readings
`examples/app-showcase` and `examples/app-crm` 0 findings; platform record pages use `placedActions: true` (not judged). HotCRM main `6090c837` 0; `v6.5.0` 3 (the card's two lead differences plus the case visibility case). These are the thread's runs; I did not re-run HotCRM.

### Nits (no hold)
- **N1.** `titleTexts` reads every string value of an object `title` as a locale; a label object with a non-locale string key would be judged too. The spec's `I18nLabel` is a string or an inline locale map, so nothing hits it today.

FINAL on the green head. No L2 is owed; the seat lands it.
